transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is my eating, especially in the evenings. I’ll stop and get, like, a family-size takeout order—more than one person would normally get—and then sometimes I’ll pick up chips or something from the bakery too. And I end up eating most of it myself before I even really notice how much is gone.

It sounds ridiculous saying it out loud. I mean, I supervise people all day, I’m organized at work, I remember everyone’s schedules and who needs what paperwork, and then I get home and it’s like… I don’t know. The food is just disappearing, and then I look down and realize what I’ve done.
After you eat that amount of food in the evening, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I feel awful afterward, and I’ll think, like, “Tomorrow I’ll do better,” but as far as making myself sick or taking something… I don’t think that’s really what I do.

Exercise, gosh, I barely get around to it consistently. I keep meaning to—there’s a gym near my office, and one of the ladies at work swears by going before her shift, but I’m usually dealing with emails before I even get there. So… no, I don’t think I do anything like that afterward.
When you're eating that large amount of food in the evening, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Yes. That’s… that’s probably the worst part. Once I start, it’s like this awful switch flips. I can be standing there thinking, Taylor, put it away, just close the container, and my hands are still opening the next thing like I’m not the one in charge.

And it’s strange because I make decisions all day long at work—people come to me for answers, you know, printer issues, schedules, someone’s timecard is wrong—and then with this, I’ll be watching myself keep eating and I can’t seem to stop it in the moment.
Do you often eat alone during these evenings because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yes… I do. I kind of arrange it that way, honestly. Like if my husband has gone to bed, that’s when it feels… safer, I guess. Or if we’ve had contractors around the house, I’ll wait until they’re gone, because the idea of someone seeing the amount I can eat is just mortifying.

It’s funny—not funny, but you know what I mean—I spend all day at work being the controlled one, the person who knows what’s going on, and then I’m hiding in the kitchen or eating after everyone’s out of sight. I would be so embarrassed if anyone actually watched it.
After these eating episodes, do you feel intense guilt, shame, or distress about how much you've eaten?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it “intense,” exactly. I definitely don’t feel good about it afterward. I’ll sort of stand there and look at the wrappers or the dishes and think, what was that, Taylor? And then I usually try to clean it up fast so it’s not sitting there staring at me.

But “shame” is a strong word… though maybe that is what it is. It’s hard to separate, because by then I’m also tired, and my feet hurt from the day, and I’m thinking about what I have to deal with tomorrow at the office—there’s always some little fire to put out, someone needing something, the copier jammed again—and I just sort of feel… disappointed in myself, I guess. Not proud of it.
How often do these eating episodes happen—do they occur at least once a week, and have they been going on like this for several months?

Yeah… yes. I actually started writing things down in this little journal—not even for this at first, it was more because I was trying to keep track of groceries and meals, and then it turned into, I don’t know, proof of what was happening.

And when I look back at it, there’s barely been a week in the last several months where there wasn’t at least one night like that. Most weeks it’s more than once. Several times, usually. I’ll tell myself on Sunday, okay, this week is going to be normal, and then by Tuesday or Wednesday I’m writing it down again.
